definitions.explanation: A type of Japanese pickle made from daikon radish that has been sun-dried and then pickled in rice bran and salt. Characterized by its yellow color and crunchy texture.

examples.japanese: {沢庵|たくあん}をご{飯|はん}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{食|た}べる。
おばあちゃんの{手作|てづく}り{沢庵|たくあん}は{絶品|ぜっぴん}だ。
{定食|ていしょく}に{沢庵|たくあん}と{味噌汁|みそしる}が{付|つ}いていた。
examples.english: The set meal came with takuan and miso soup.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Named after the Zen Buddhist monk {沢庵宗彭|たくあんそうほう} (1573-1645), who is traditionally credited with popularizing this pickling method. {沢庵|たくあん} is one of the most common {漬物|つけもの} (pickles) in Japan, typically served as a side dish with rice. The bright yellow color comes from rice bran ({糠|ぬか}) fermentation or sometimes from turmeric.

Also written in hiragana as たくあん or katakana as タクアン.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {沢庵|たくあん}{漬|づ}け: takuan pickles (formal name)
- {沢庵|たくあん}を{漬|つ}ける: to pickle takuan
- {沢庵|たくあん}を{切|き}る: to slice takuan
